assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only mushoku-tensei:rudeus@light-novel#character-model (MT_RUDEUS_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL revision 1.12, canonical, BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL), #monograph-v01-v10 and #monograph-v01-v15 (the two canonical Rudeus monographs, version 1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked Japanese light novels V01-V15. The model and monographs route source observations to an evidence index, a shared state ledger, sequential readings and checkpoints, none of which is curated on this subject or used as evidence here. The model's own readiness label is a method input, not a conclusion adopted here. Diary, elder testimony and Orsted's reincarnation account are attributed accounts. No web novel, later light-novel volume, adaptation, performed voice, reception or remembered franchise biography is in scope.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Japanese light novels V01-V15, through selector MT-RM-ST55 (spoken marriage, renewed concealment, identity disclosure and negotiated service). Each claim applies only to a named selector's knowledge; the V01-V10 monograph stays frozen at V10; no earlier state acquires later knowledge, and the origin account is still undisclosed to Roxy and Sylphiette at the boundary. Nothing after V15 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model states nine conditional rules (MT-RM-001 to 009), each with trigger, knowledge and relationship conditions, competing motives, a supported response range, countercases and a falsifier: practical learning (001), impression control under apparently manageable risk (003), fear conditioned on credible threat, felt control and access to correction (004), salience-bounded care (005) and consultation as a selectable process (008). The monographs explain the underlying wish for a useful life with enduring attachments and the conditional arranging of another person's response (V02:003, V03:012-018, V10:003/007/018). B is rejected because the model rates mechanism confidence moderate, gives response ranges rather than selections, assigns no priority between care and control, and says outright that recognizing reasons does not ensure honoring them (MT-RM-005, V15 extension); the variable that would decide his choice is left open. D is rejected because explicit conditional rules with falsifiers plus two monographs exceed distributed description.

The model distinguishes 55 analytical state selectors (MT-RM-ST01 to ST55) from V01 accompanied learning to V15 negotiated service, each with active conditions and a knowledge or constraint column, and extends every rule volume by volume through V15 with 87 retrospective checks. The monographs supply the V01-V10 argument frozen at its boundary and the V11-V15 extension (Norn repair, Paul's death, fatherhood, diary, coercion, rescue, employment). A is rejected because the selectors are retrospective analytical states, not a validated transition model, the V01-V10 and V01-V15 monographs are syntheses rather than state-by-state readings, and the model says gains in one domain leave another vulnerable without stating when a state change transfers. C is rejected because explicit per-volume selectors with knowledge limits exceed a sequence described only in prose.

MT-RM-009 operationalizes his written register: polite boku and honorific presentation for access, rough ore as performed toughness, an inner diction more self-mocking, sexualized and game-laden than courteous dialogue, and directness as a wish to drop the performance, located across V02-V15 (for example V07:011-012/021-023 invited boku-to-ore shift, V09:017/026 requested informal address, V10:007/018 plain-apology request). The V01-V10 monograph analyzes interior versus spoken register (V07:025, V09:030-032, V10:007/026/030-034). B is rejected because the model states it is not a mechanical pronoun classifier, no wording beyond the pronouns is quoted, and register is never a truth or consent certificate; it gives contrasts, not an idiolect. D is rejected because a stated register rule with located contrasts and countercases exceeds prose characterization.

The model's ordinary-behavior section names constraints (fatigue from processing materials, money anxiety, food preference, interest in magical experiments, embarrassment, wish for group belonging, practical questions) and says they suffice for restrained near analogies about a shared purchase or lesson; MT-RM-001 and the V04-V15 check rows add letters, meal planning, recipe dependence, paid repair, classes, library inquiry and childcare. The monographs treat ordinary tasks as central evidence (V07:003-010/015-019, V13:007/011/013, V15:029-031). B is rejected because the model explicitly excludes every leisure preference, an adult domestic persona, modern institutional literacy and universal cultural expertise, and calls domestic conduct bounded choices rather than reliable marriage conduct. D is rejected because stated ordinary constraints with an admitted near-analog range exceed described patterns.

The model conditions behavior on role and recipient: learner cooperation (002), a person-specific Ruijerd reciprocity rule (007) that it refuses to generalize, temporary nonleader versus leader roles (008, V07 revision), and a relationship section for Roxy, Eris, Ruijerd, Hitogami and strangers; selectors record relation-specific knowledge such as Eris's intention being unavailable in ST15. The monographs differentiate Roxy, Eris, Paul, Norn, Sylphiette, Nanahoshi, Zanoba, Cliff, Juli, Sara and Orsted (V11:007-011, V15:011-012). B is rejected because only Ruijerd has a recipient-specific rule, the model lists adult relationships as insufficient evidence, and most wife, sibling and colleague conduct appears as check rows rather than conditioned rules. D is rejected because role-conditioned rules and differentiated located relations exceed a relational sketch.

The model treats represented interiority and attributed reports as D0 DIRECT evidence and selectors bound what he knows, for example Norn's internal account being reader knowledge rather than his (ST39). The monographs analyze his narration as resource and defense: candid revision coexists with explanation substituted for change, and correcting the diary's suspicion of Eris does not remove the expectation behind a new misreading (V14:013/017/027, V15:006/025). B is rejected because the model does not map interior states to conditions beyond fear (004) and recognized-but-unheeded reasons, and the reader often learns reasons he never has. D is rejected because located, critically bounded interior access exceeds inference from behavior.

MT-RM-004 conditions fear and recovery under credible threat, MT-RM-006 is a tightly scoped protective-entrapment rule kept UNTESTED outside V03, and check rows locate the V08 retaliation, the V14 lethal escape attempt, the V15 armor defeat and coercive bargain (V14:018-021, V15:014-015/019-024). The monographs exclude both a coward label and a mastermind reading. B is rejected because the model states high-stakes judgment has diagnostic failure evidence, not operational reliability, and refuses to broaden 006 into all danger. D is rejected because conditioned conflict rules with countercases exceed located disputes alone.

The monographs render weighing under Hitogami's coercion and knowing pressure on Nanahoshi despite understanding her gratitude (V15:010-012/015), and distinguish involuntary difficulty from conduct; the model's 005 rule and checks V80-V87 record that sympathy coexists with instrumental pressure and that the V10 same-person boundary recurrence disconfirms any durable transfer claim. B is rejected because the model lists sustained boundary respect as insufficient evidence and the strongest evidence shows recognized reasons failing to govern action; there is no operational rule for when deliberation prevails. D is rejected because rendered deliberation at located choices exceeds positions alone.

The evidence locates comic, game-inflected and self-mocking diction in narration (MT-RM-009, V13 comic speculation) and the role of comic presentation around bodily boundaries (V01:011-012, V13:015/020, V15:004/025/028), mainly as a reading problem that can soften misconduct. D is rejected because humor is located as narrative register, not as characterized joking or play with others; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the comic register is located.

Three curated items cover the whole authorized corpus V01-V15: two canonical monographs with dense VNN:NNN locators and a living model with per-volume revisions 1.1 to 1.12 and retrospective checks. B is rejected because the model and monographs both defer source observations to the evidence index, shared ledger and sequential readings, none of which is curated on this subject, and all checks are retrospective fits under declared prior franchise exposure. D is rejected because sustained specialist coverage of every authorized volume exceeds distributed evidence.

Every rule carries an explicit countercase and falsifier, and the model distinguishes UNTESTED from passed (002 in V07, V14 and V15; 006 and 007 from V07 on), says a missing trigger cannot count as a successful prediction, and records that the V10 public-touch recurrence disconfirms durable universal transfer. The monographs add located limits: the staged and delayed rescue, harm to the captives, teaching failures, false transfer from competence to authority, recurring concealment of the Orsted visit and knowing pressure on Nanahoshi. A is rejected because the checks are retrospective, not blinded holdouts, and the model excludes generated sexualized tests, so some limits remain untested. C is rejected because rule-level falsifiers and explicit UNTESTED dispositions exceed limits argued only in prose.

The model binds every rule extension to named selectors, states that no earlier state acquires later knowledge, and specifies when information becomes available (the V05 disclosure supplies family information in ST09-10; Nanahoshi's identity is known from ST30; Roxy and Sylphiette remain uninformed of the rebirth account in ST55). It keeps physical age, elapsed second-life experience, remembered first-life biography and social treatment separate. The monographs freeze the V01-V10 argument and treat the elder's testimony and diary as attributed. A is rejected because selectors carry no elapsed times or ages and the V03/V04 to V15 extensions are applied rule by rule rather than through a calendar. C is rejected because explicit knowledge availability per selector exceeds volume-level bounding.

scenario_readiness.note: MT-RM-009 gives register contrasts and the model treats written public/private register as BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL, but it is not a pronoun classifier, quotes no wording beyond pronouns, excludes performed voice, and register predicts neither truth nor content. CONDITIONAL would license generated lines whose fluency would outrun the located contrasts; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the stated register rule.

conditions: One named selector from MT-RM-ST01 to ST55, with only that selector's knowledge; diary, elder testimony and Orsted's reincarnation account remain attributed and never supply later knowledge or powers.

Only the model's BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL domains: practical learning and coordination, familiar-party interaction and written public/private register; high-stakes judgment, sustained boundary respect, adult relationships, unfamiliar politics, prophecy and audiovisual delivery require abstention.
Output is a labeled hypothetical response range under the applicable rule, with its countercase and falsifier; it never asserts that recognizing a reason will govern his action.
No sexualized scenario and no invented source quotation; modern-setting extrapolation and unseen diplomacy are out of scope.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A single selector within Japanese light novels V01-V15 with that state's knowledge only; nothing after V15; the V01-V10 monograph's argument for states up to V10.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Attested recipients in their selector-specific relation, such as Roxy, Eris, Sylphiette, Paul, Norn, Aisha, Ruijerd, Zanoba, Cliff, Juli, Nanahoshi, Sara, Elinalise and Orsted; Ruijerd's reciprocity rule is not generalized to others.

scenario_readiness.note: The model permits only D1 NEAR_ANALOG reconstruction within each rule's named conditions and sets the procedure for a near analogy: state the money knowledge, available experts, stakes and selector, and allow several plausible choices. READY is rejected because mechanism confidence is moderate, all domains are BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL with abstention outside them, and checks are retrospective; NOT_READY is rejected because the model explicitly admits bounded near-analog output in its provisional domains.

conditions: Only familiar-party practical errands, study, chores, meals and lessons as near analogs of located scenes, with the selector, money knowledge, available experts and stakes stated.
Several plausible choices are allowed; no invented leisure preference, household routine or adult domestic persona.
Recipients keep independent decisions; his consent or permission practice is never inferred from familiarity.
Behavior is described in prose; no quoted speech is generated as canonical.
scenario_readiness.note: The model's ordinary-behavior section says its constraints suffice for restrained near analogies about a shared purchase or lesson, and MT-RM-001 and 008 cover practical coordination with familiar parties. READY is rejected because the model excludes leisure preferences, an adult domestic persona and reliable marriage conduct; NOT_READY is rejected because the model admits this narrow range explicitly.

The model states that high-stakes judgment has diagnostic failure evidence, not operational reliability, and that no rule ensures recognized reasons are honored; the monographs' central finding is pressure despite accurate understanding (V15:011-012). CONDITIONAL would turn an explanatory account into a prediction; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the rendered deliberation.

The model lists sustained boundary respect and adult relationships as insufficient evidence, forbids generated sexualized scenarios, and records the V10 same-person boundary recurrence as disconfirming durable transfer; the monographs keep refusal and assent distinct (V10:007-010/015/018/025, V15:004/025/028). CONDITIONAL would generate intimate conduct where the evidence affirmatively shows recurring boundary failures; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the located record.

conditions: Only tutoring a familiar learner whose cooperation matters, or technical research, craft or party work with collaborators, as near analogs of located V02-V13 scenes with the selector stated.
The learner's or collaborator's independent knowledge and decisions are preserved; compliance from a dependent is not cooperative consent, and successful instruction is not emancipation.
No ordinary employment under Orsted, mission performance, institutional politics or universal teaching method is assumed.
Behavior is described in prose; no quoted speech is generated as canonical.
scenario_readiness.note: MT-RM-001, 002 and 008 cover practical learning, tutoring a familiar learner and consultation in research or party work, inside the model's BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL learning and practical-coordination domain, with direct tests from V02, V08, V09 and V10 (V08:013-016/030, V10:016). READY is rejected because 002 has no comparable sustained tutoring test after V13, competence repeatedly fails to transfer to authority, and Orsted employment is untested; NOT_READY is rejected because located tutoring, research and craft collaboration are admitted.

known_limits.statement: The model is BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL in every admitted domain, marks no domain DOMAIN_READY, rates mechanism confidence moderate and requires abstention in unsupported contexts; the V01-V15 monograph calls the account explanatory constraints, not a validated simulator.

Recognizing another person's need or objection does not reliably govern his next action; accurate empathy can coexist with deliberate pressure, as with Nanahoshi in V15, and no rule ensures recognized reasons are honored.

A stated boundary was violated again after he acknowledged it (V10), which the model treats as disconfirming any durable universal transfer; earlier refusals remain refusals after later closeness and marriage creates no universal access.
Technical capacity does not confer knowledge of others' needs or comprehensive authority, and high output does not make him a capable teacher of every learner.

Impression control applies to specific opportunities under apparently manageable risk; not every gift, joke, plan or act of aid conceals exploitation, and V15 concealment is a near analogy rather than the original staged-rescue trigger.
Register shifts are contrasts, not a pronoun classifier, and neither politeness nor rough speech certifies truth, disclosure or consent.

The older self's diary, the elder's testimony and Orsted's reincarnation account are attributed accounts; they cannot supply young Rudeus with future powers or serve as verified chronology or cosmology.
Rules 006 and 007 are UNTESTED under their exact triggers after V03 and V06, and rule 002 has no comparable sustained tutoring test in V14 or V15; untested is not passed.
All 87 checks are retrospective fits under declared prior franchise exposure: no clean holdout, numerical forecast or clinical diagnosis follows.

The evidence index, shared state ledger, sequential readings and checkpoints that own the source observations are not curated on this subject; locators are known here only as the model and monographs route them. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
No wording beyond pronoun contrasts and no acoustic performance is in evidence.

Nothing after V15 is assessed; whether his capacity to accept correction holds under another threat, ordinary service under Orsted and his disclosure of the origin account to Roxy and Sylphiette remain open.

assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Japanese light novels V01-V15, the authorized terminal volume: the V01-V10 monograph is a historical argument frozen at its V10 boundary, and the V01-V15 monograph extends it through V11 (Norn), V12 (Paul's death and Zenith's impairment), V13 (fatherhood, the Sara meeting), V14 and V15 (the diary, Hitogami's coercion, the ambush, the rescue, the Orsted employment terms and the marriage to Eris). The curated evidence gives no state selectors; states are named only by volume and source locator. assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monographs give a sustained, located explanation: a wish for a useful life with enduring attachments, pursued through practiced competence, alongside shame and fear that make others' interpretations hard to bear; a conditional tendency to arrange a desired response before the other person understands the arrangement, explicitly limited so that not all aid counts as exploitation (V02:003, V03:012-018, V10:003/007/018); fear conditioned on credible threat, felt control, the relationship and access to correction; and recognized reasons that do not always govern action (V15:011-012). They name the model's rules 001-009 and state the conditions under which each applies or must not absorb a case. B is not supported because the operational rules and selectors live in the uncurated model, and the V01-V15 monograph calls its account explanatory constraints, not a validated simulator, with scene evidence stronger than mechanism generalization; specialist explanation with conditions and countercases exceeds distributed description, so D is not supported.

Two time-bounded syntheses trace development as an expanding but unevenly selected set of practices rather than a continuous rise: V01-V10 instruction, teaching, travel, school and the V10 marriage, and V11-V15 the Norn repair, Paul's death, fatherhood, the diary, coercion, rescue and bounded employment. The later monograph preserves the earlier argument at its historical scope and says gains in one domain leave another vulnerable. B is not supported because the curated evidence has no state selectors, the 55 states belong to the uncurated model and states are identified only by volume and locator; a sequence across fifteen volumes with explicit non-transfer between states exceeds an undifferentiated profile, so D is not supported.

The V01-V10 monograph characterizes his written voice in prose: internal narration with comic, game-inflected and sexualized comparisons that can hurry past another person's cost, a courteous spoken presentation that often differs from the interior register as audience-sensitive performance, and narration repeatedly supplemented by other accounts (V07:025, V09:030-032, V10:007/026/030-034); the later monograph adds his goddess categories for his wives (V15:016/028/033-035). The row limits speech to written narration and self-presentation. C is not supported because no wording or self-reference is quoted and the register is not operationalized; a differentiated interior-versus-spoken register with located contrasts exceeds a bare prose label, so E is not supported.

The monographs treat ordinary tasks as central evidence: shopping, studying, preparing materials, discussing equipment, cleaning and housekeeping, imperfect shares of chores, school duties and research during distress (V07:003-010/015-019), fatherhood as practices learned with other caregivers (V13:007/011/013) and asking Orsted for family time and pay (V15:029-031). C is not supported because these are described as patterns of work rather than modeled conditions, and the rules that would operationalize them are in the uncurated model; described practices across many volumes exceed a single mention, so E is not supported.

The monographs differentiate many recipients: Roxy as formative teacher and idealized figure; Eris as learner, companion and independent agent whose meanings he misreads, and later wife who assents, worries and apologizes; Ruijerd's unpaid protection; Paul's mutual misreading and local repair; Norn, whose trust his competence cannot require (V11:007-011); Sylphiette's small explicit corrections and later objection; Nanahoshi as collaborator he knowingly pressures (V15:011-012); Zanoba, Cliff, Juli, Sara and Orsted. Each relation is bounded by what he can know. B is not supported because the treatment is interpretive prose without recipient-conditioned rules in the evidence set; differentiated, located responses across many recipients exceed a single relational sketch, so D is not supported.

The monographs draw on narration that gives immediate access to embarrassment, fear, ingenuity and desire, and analyze his self-account as both resource and defense: he can revise a label or admit a motive he dislikes while substituting explanation for changed action, and correcting the diary's suspicion of Eris does not remove the expectation behind a new mistake (V14:013/017/027, V15:006/025). They also bar treating narration as either absolution or uniformly deceptive and supplement it with others' accounts. B is not supported because interior access is analyzed rather than mapped to conditions, and the reader often learns reasons he never has (V11:007-011); located, critically bounded interior access exceeds inference from behavior alone, so D is not supported.

The monographs locate conflict conduct with countercases: staged danger and a delayed rescue that ends in a child's death (V02:003, V03:012-018), coordinated harm against constrained captives despite heard objection (V08:019-025), a recurring public-touch violation after Sylphiette's stated boundary (V10:007-010/015/018/025), decision under Hitogami's coercion, knowing pressure on Nanahoshi, and the ambush his friends' work affects though the battle is lost (V15:010-015/019). They exclude both a coward label and a mastermind reading. B is not supported because the conditions are argued in prose and the operational rules are uncurated; located conflict trajectories with conditions and countercases exceed located disputes alone, so D is not supported.

The monographs analyze rendered weighing: obedience to Hitogami as a decision under coercion, narrowed by perceived reach and fear of family loss, while he knows the god may lie (V15:010/015); pressing Nanahoshi while accurately understanding that helping the ambush violates her gratitude, which defeats a learned-empathy thesis (V15:011-012); recognition that interrupts harm without becoming a governing habit (V02:009/014 to V09:019/024); and the distinction between involuntary difficulty and conduct. B is not supported because the account is interpretive, the monograph calls it not a validated simulator and the strongest evidence shows recognized reasons failing to govern action; rendered deliberation with located choices exceeds positions alone, so D is not supported.

The monographs name comic and game-inflected comparisons in his narration and the role of comic presentation around bodily boundaries (V01:011-012, V13:015/020, V15:004/025/028), mainly as a reading problem that can soften misconduct, without a pattern of his joking or play. D is not supported because humor is located as narrative register rather than characterized behavior; located comic register exceeds silence, so NOT_ASSESSED would ignore it.

Two curated canonical monographs cover the whole authorized corpus V01-V15 with dense VNN:NNN locators, explicit strongest alternatives and open tests. C rather than B because both monographs defer operational rules, state selectors and observations to the model, evidence index and ledgers, none of which is curated on the row; they disclaim clinical diagnosis, a complete adult persona, DOMAIN_READY status and a clean holdout. Sustained specialist coverage of every authorized volume exceeds distributed evidence, so D is not supported.

The monographs locate affirmative limits: a staged rescue and a delayed rescue ending in a child's death, a childhood refusal that later affection does not erase, harm to the captives, a recurring boundary violation, teaching failures with Zanoba and inability to acquire Sylphiette's healing, a false transfer from technical competence to authority, recurring concealment of the Orsted visit after a demand for openness, and knowing pressure on Nanahoshi. They state that these defeat a decisive-moral-conversion reading and that a missing trigger cannot count as a successful prediction. B is not supported because the limits are argued in prose without the model's calibration rows in the evidence set; located failures and recurrences across fifteen volumes exceed bare gap statements, so D is not supported.

The evidence binds claims to volumes and locators and keeps knowledge time-bound: the V01-V10 argument stays frozen at its boundary, the elder's testimony cannot supply young Rudeus with future powers, the diary's gaps prevent it from functioning as a transparent future, the origin account is an attributed inference that still changes his state, and disclosure to Roxy and Sylphiette is pending at V15. B is not supported because no selectors, ages or elapsed times are in the evidence set; D is not supported because knowledge and claims are bounded per volume rather than given as a loose period.

scenario_readiness.note: The monographs characterize his narration and spoken presentation only in prose, quote no wording and state that illustrations do not verify performed voice. CONDITIONAL would generate speech from interpretive prose; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the characterized register.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A single named volume state within V01-V15 with that volume's knowledge only; the V01-V10 argument for states up to V10, nothing after V15, and diary or elder testimony never treated as his accomplished past or future.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Only attested recipients in their volume-specific relation: Roxy, Eris, Sylphiette, Paul, Zenith, Norn, Aisha, Ruijerd, Zanoba, Cliff, Nanahoshi, Juli, Sara, Orsted and Hitogami.

scenario_readiness.note: The V01-V15 monograph states that its account is explanatory constraints, not a validated simulator of arbitrary situations, that all domains remain BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL, that unsupported contexts require abstention and that whether his capacity for correction becomes reliable under another threat is left open. CONDITIONAL would build novel-scenario behavior from interpretation without the uncurated operational model; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the explicit application bounds.

Ordinary work, chores, study, caregiving and employment terms are described as patterns in interpretive prose without modeled conditions in the evidence set. CONDITIONAL would build ordinary social behavior from description; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the substantial ordinary material the monographs locate.

The evidence renders his deliberation under coercion and his knowing pressure on Nanahoshi, but its central finding is that recognized reasons do not reliably govern action, and the monograph disclaims simulation. CONDITIONAL would turn an explanatory account into a predictive one; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the rendered deliberation.

Romantic and marital material is extensive and affirmatively limiting: earlier refusals remain refusals after later closeness, marriage creates no universal access, a stated boundary is violated again (V10:007-010/015/018/025), and V15 intimacy with Eris contains both assent and tension over force and pace (V15:004/025/028). The monographs refuse to collapse refusal and assent and claim no complete adult persona. CONDITIONAL would generate intimate conduct where the evidence shows recurring boundary failures and no operational rule; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the located record.

Teaching, research, technical preparation and employment are located (V02:006-011, V08:013-016, V10:016, V15:014-015/029-031), but the evidence stresses that high output does not make him a capable teacher of every learner, that competence falsely transfers to authority, and that the rules for learning, teaching and collaboration live in the uncurated model, with no new sustained teaching trial in V15. CONDITIONAL would supply an operational procedure the evidence set does not contain; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore the located professional material.

known_limits.statement: The V01-V15 monograph states that its account is explanatory constraints, not a validated simulator; scene evidence is stronger than mechanism generalization, and all domains remain BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL with abstention in unsupported contexts.
Recognizing another person's need or objection does not reliably govern his next action; accurate empathy can coexist with deliberate pressure, as with Nanahoshi in V15.
Technical capacity does not confer knowledge of others' needs or comprehensive authority, and high magical output does not make him a capable teacher of every learner.
His tendency to arrange a desired response applies to specific opportunities under apparently manageable risk; not every gift, joke, plan or act of aid conceals exploitation.

Earlier refusals remain refusals after later closeness, marriage creates no universal access, and a stated boundary was violated again after he acknowledged it; comic presentation does not remove the affected person's response.

The older self's diary, the elder's testimony and Orsted's reincarnation account are attributed accounts; they cannot supply young Rudeus with future powers or serve as verified chronology or cosmology.
Neither a decisive moral conversion at V15 nor a reading in which every gain is selfish control fits the evidence; concealment recurs and correction is also accepted.
Prior franchise familiarity is declared, so retrospective fit is not clean prediction, and no DOMAIN_READY status or clinical diagnosis follows.

The Rudeus reconstruction model (revision 1.12, nine rules, 55 states, 87 checks), the evidence index, the shared ledgers, the readings and the checkpoints are not curated on this subject; rule and state claims are known here only as the monographs report them. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
No wording, self-reference or acoustic performance is in evidence; register is described only in prose.
Nothing after V15 is assessed; whether his capacity to accept correction holds under another threat is left open, and his disclosure to Roxy and Sylphiette is pending.
